comparison: Both evaluate claims C69, C70, C89, C90 about the mechanistic model integrating structural observations with degron-length experiments. OpenEval finds the model well-supported by convergent structural and biochemical evidence. Peer reviewers also support this mechanistic interpretation without raising concerns.

Both address claims C46-C48, C51-C54, C95-C96 about integration of structural findings with prior biochemical data. OpenEval finds strong support from convergence of new biochemical data with structural observations and prior literature. Peer reviewers agree, noting the structure successfully rationalizes extensive previous mutagenesis and specificity studies.

Both evaluate claims C61, C62, C97, C100 about the closed-channel recognition mechanism. OpenEval finds the mechanistic inferences well-supported by structural observations and prior biochemical data. Peer reviewers also support this functional interpretation without challenge.

Both address claims C35-C36 about comparisons with prior structural studies. OpenEval finds reasonable inferences supported by observation of unique side-chain density (C34). Peer reviewers mark as uncertain, requesting more detailed explanation of how current work differs from and advances on prior publications.

Both evaluate claims C37-C43 about specific molecular interactions from cryo-EM data. OpenEval finds detailed structural observations internally consistent and well-supported by density maps. Peer reviewers support the structural observations, noting biochemical validation experiments were accepted without objection, though they requested close-ups of cryo-EM maps with fitted models.

Both address claims C77-C80, C84 about degron-length dependence experiments and modeling. OpenEval finds clear experimental data with well-supported conclusions integrating structural and biochemical data. Peer reviewers also support these findings without raising concerns.

Both evaluate claims C9, C73-C74 about generalization to other AAA+ machines and molecular motors. OpenEval marks as uncertain, noting speculative nature and lack of direct experimental evidence for other systems. Peer reviewers support the claims, noting appropriate framing as speculative and logical connection to findings.

Both address claims C85-C86 about nucleotide states. OpenEval finds structural observations well-supported by cryo-EM data and consistency with prior work. Peer reviewers mark as uncertain, explicitly requesting close-ups of cryo-EM maps for all nucleotide-binding sites and stating readers cannot accept the information at face value.

Both evaluate claims C87-C88 about mechanistic interpretation of nucleotide states and conformational transitions. OpenEval finds good support from structural data and consistency with prior single-molecule work, though notes C87 remains speculative. Peer reviewers support this interpretation without challenge, noting appropriate framing as plausible.

Both address claims C55-C56, C59 about the intermediate complex structure. OpenEval finds convergent and well-supported evidence with consistency to prior AAA+ structural studies. Peer reviewers also support these structural observations without challenge.

Both evaluate claims C5, C27-C28, C33 about cryo-EM structures of two distinct complexes. OpenEval finds convergent structural evidence with well-documented resolution and features. Peer reviewers mark as uncertain, requesting additional cryo-EM data presentation including local resolution maps, close-ups, and details on data quality and processing strategy.

Both address claims C44-C45, C49-C50 about new biochemical validation experiments. OpenEval finds new experimental data directly validates structural observations with strong support. Peer reviewers mark as uncertain, requesting statistics for Figure 3A to indicate which differences are and are not significant.

Both evaluate claims C91-C93 about novelty of the recognition complex structure. OpenEval finds novelty established by comparison with prior structures. Peer reviewers support the structural novelty as a key distinguishing finding, though they requested better explanation of differences from prior studies.

Both address claims C105-C106 about cryo-EM data processing methodology. OpenEval finds methodological details support quality of structures. Peer reviewers mark as uncertain, requesting supplementary figure showing full processing pipeline, different structures from 3D classification, and particle numbers at each step.

OpenEval evaluates claims C29-C32, C108-C109 about structural features and nucleotide occupancy comparisons, finding straightforward structural observations well-supported by cryo-EM data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1-C26 about established background knowledge, finding well-established context supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are background claims rather than new findings.

OpenEval evaluates claims C60, C71-C72 about integration of prior functional work with current structural findings, finding well-supported connections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific integration claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C63-C68 about integration with prior kinetic studies, finding well-reasoned connections despite some speculative aspects (C67). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific kinetic integration claims.

Peer reviewers evaluate claim C34 about comparison with prior structures, requesting more detailed explanation of differences. This claim appears in OpenEval R1 but is not the primary focus of that evaluation, which centers on C5, C27-C28, C33.
